## 背景

`tests/perf/load_test.js` 由 `qa-test-runner` 容器内的 k6 执行，被测目标为同一台宿主机上的 Prism Mock 服务（`qa-mock-service:4010`），两者共享宿主机 CPU / 内存与 Docker 虚拟网桥 `qa-infra-net`。

## 影响

1. **压测结果失真**：压测发起端与被测端在同一台机器、同一个 Docker 网桥上，测得的 p95 延迟几乎只反映容器间回环开销，无法代表真实网络 RTT。
2. **资源竞争**：k6、PostgreSQL、Prism、Allure 共享宿主机 CPU / 内存，压测期间的结果会受同机其他容器负载干扰，缺乏可复现性。
3. **无横向扩展能力**：k6 单实例受限于单机文件描述符、CPU 与网卡带宽，无法模拟真实生产级高并发流量。
4. **定位不清**：当前实现只适合作为**性能基线（Smoke Load Test）**，但文档中未明确这一边界，容易被误读为具备生产级压测能力。

## 建议方案

**短期（明确边界）**

- 在 `tests/perf/`、README、USER_GUIDE 中明确标注：本套件仅为**本地性能基线 / 冒烟级压测**，不作为容量评估依据
- 输出中显式记录执行环境（单机容器），避免结果被误用

**中期（可观测性）**

- 接入 Prometheus + Grafana 采集 k6 指标（k6 原生支持 `--out experimental-prometheus-rw`），把结果落到时序库而非仅控制台输出，便于横向对比历史基线

**长期（分布式压测）**

- 采用 k6 Operator（Kubernetes）或 `k6 run --execution-segment` 分片，在多台机器上分布式执行
- 或引入可横向扩展的方案（Locust 分布式模式 / k6 Cloud），使压测节点与被测服务物理隔离

## 验收标准

- [ ] 文档中明确标注当前压测能力边界（基线级，非生产级）
- [ ] 压测输出中包含执行环境说明
- [ ] （可选）提供分布式压测的接入方案文档或 PoC
title: [压测] k6 与被测服务同机同网桥，仅能做性能基线，无法替代分布式压测

- [ ] Create TanStack Query hooks in `app/src/hooks/` (one per contract `operationId`, e.g., `useSearchStudents`, `useStudentById`, `useStudentReviews`, `useCreateReview`, `useAskChatbot`, `useApprovalQueueItems`, `useDecideApplications`, `useDepartments`, `usePrograms`, `useAuditLogs`) calling `apiClient` and `request()` from `app/src/lib/api`.

- [ ] Wire at least **one designed failure state** so it is reachable and demonstrable live in the UI against Prism:
  - e.g., `POST /functions/v1/reviews` returning `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`REVIEW_WORD_LIMIT` when exceeding 500 words or `REVIEW_BODY_REQUIRED`), OR
  - e.g., `POST /functions/v1/chat` returning `429 Too Many Requests` (`RATE_LIMITED`) and rendering the graceful retry prompt with `error.hint`.

- **Allowed:** Requests configured via `configureApiAuth` (attaching `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `apikey` headers) succeed against Prism's `200`/`201`/`204` responses.

- `ApiRequestError` instances thrown by `request()` in `app/src/lib/api/request.ts` are caught by TanStack Query / form handlers and display `error.message` and `error.hint`.

Is a Monorepo a Good Idea Here? **Yes — for VineMe's architecture, a monorepo is a strong fit**, provided a few Expo + Next.js workspace gotchas are handled upfront. ### Why it works well for VineMe 1. **Single Source of Truth for Supabase (`supabase/`)**: Both the Expo mobile app and the Next.js web app (marketing site + church admin dashboard) query the same Supabase database, RLS policies, RPC functions (e.g., `get_user_contact_admin`), and Edge Functions (`sync-churchsuite-vulnerable-tags`, `create-referred-user`, etc.). Keeping migrations, seeds, and Edge Functions at the repo root prevents schema drift. 2. **Shared Database & Domain Types (`packages/shared`)**: Currently, the mobile app manually maintains [`src/types/database.ts`](file:///Users/jacob/Programming/VineMe/vineme2.0/src/types/database.ts) while `vineme-website` maintains its own types in `lib/dashboard/types.ts` and `lib/dashboard/queries.ts`. With a shared package, you can run `supabase gen types typescript` once at the root and consume exact types in both apps. 3. **Unified Deep-Link & Auth Assets (`.well-known`)**: The mobile repo currently has a [`public/.well-known`](file:///Users/jacob/Programming/VineMe/vineme2.0/public/.well-known/README.md) directory with `apple-app-site-association` and `assetlinks.json` that must be served by `vineme.app`. Moving these into the Next.js app (`apps/web/public/.well-known`) means your web deployment automatically serves mobile Universal Links / App Links. 4. **Atomic Full-Stack PRs**: Features that span a database migration, an Edge Function, the church admin web dashboard, and the mobile app can be developed, reviewed, and merged in a single branch/PR. ### Key Gotchas & How We Will Avoid Them > [!WARNING] > **React 19 Version Mismatch (Expo vs. Next.js)** > - Mobile (`vineme-mobile-app`, Expo SDK 54 / RN 0.81.5) uses **`react@19.1.0`** and **`react-dom@19.1.0`**. > - Web (`vineme-website`, Next.js 16.2.4) uses **`react@19.2.4`** and **`react-dom@19.2.4`**. > > React Native's renderer strictly checks the `react` minor/patch version (`19.1.0`). If a package manager hoists two different React versions, Metro or Jest can fail with duplicate React / invalid hook call errors. > **Mitigation**: Either pin `apps/web` to `react@19.1.0` / `react-dom@19.1.0` (fully compatible with Next.js 16) **or** configure workspace resolution + `metro.config.js` blockList/extraNodeModules so `apps/mobile` always resolves its own React instance. --- ## 2. Audit of Current Repo Clutter (`vineme2.0`) Before restructuring, the following clutter in the repository root should be cleaned up: | Item | Issue | Proposed Action | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **`*.svg` & `*.png` in root (39 files, ~10 MB)** | Hash-named files (e.g., `cc0e9e966af016bcc53ff55e7c7553dc55df0037.png` at 8.1 MB, `00142d84...svg`) accidentally committed in `02b723e6`. Zero references across the entire codebase. | **Delete all 39 files** (`git rm`). | | **[`doc/`](file:///Users/jacob/Programming/VineMe/vineme2.0/doc/doc-script.js) & [`supabase/doc/`](file:///Users/jacob/Programming/VineMe/vineme2.0/supabase/doc/doc-script.js)** | Generated when someone accidentally ran the `docker` npm doc-generator package (`npx docker`) instead of Docker CLI. | **Delete both folders** (`git rm -r doc supabase/doc`). | | **[`cursor_github_issues_creation.md`](file:///Users/jacob/Programming/VineMe/vineme2.0/cursor_github_issues_creation.md)** | 61 KB exported Cursor chat log in the repo root (committed on current branch in `0449977a`). | **Delete** (or move to `docs/` if you want to keep it). | | **[`churchsuite-openapi.json`](file:///Users/jacob/Programming/VineMe/vineme2.0/churchsuite-openapi.json)** | 1 MB ChurchSuite OpenAPI spec sitting in the repo root. | **Move to `mocks/churchsuite-openapi.json`** (and optionally point `docker-compose.yml` Prism mock at the local file so it works offline). | | **[`FONT_SETUP.md`](file:///Users/jacob/Programming/VineMe/vineme2.0/FONT_SETUP.md)** | Setup doc sitting in the root directory. | **Move to `docs/mobile/font-setup.md`**. | | **[`public/.well-known/`](file:///Users/jacob/Programming/VineMe/vineme2.0/public/.well-known/apple-app-site-association) & [`public/auth/`](file:///Users/jacob/Programming/VineMe/vineme2.0/public/auth/verify-email.html)** | Universal links & static email verification fallback meant to be hosted on `vineme.app`. | **Move into `apps/web/public/`** so Next.js serves them on the production domain. | | **Mobile [`package.json`](file:///Users/jacob/Programming/VineMe/vineme2.0/package.json) dependencies** | `eas-cli` is in `dependencies` (bloating installs); `express` and `body-parser` are in root `dependencies` (only needed by `mocks/`). | Move `eas-cli` to `devDependencies` and remove unused `express`/`body-parser` from mobile app. | --- ## 3. Target Monorepo Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD Root["vineme (Monorepo Root)
package.json (npm workspaces) + turbo.json"] Root --> Apps["apps/"] Root --> Packages["packages/"] Root --> Supabase["supabase/"] Root --> Mocks["mocks/"] Root --> Docs["docs/"] Apps --> Mobile["apps/mobile
(Expo / React Native App)"] Apps --> Web["apps/web
(Next.js 16 Website & Admin Dashboard)"] Packages --> Shared["packages/shared
(@vineme/shared: DB Types & Constants)"] Mobile -.->|imports| Shared Web -.->|imports| Shared Supabase -.->|generates types into| Shared ``` ### Target Directory Layout ```text vineme2.0/ ├── package.json # Root workspace config + Turborepo / convenience scripts ├── turbo.json # Fast parallel task runner (dev, build, lint, typecheck, test) ├── docker-compose.yml # Local ChurchSuite Prism mock + custom mocks container ├── apps/ │ ├── mobile/ # Current Expo app (moved via git mv to preserve history) │ │ ├── app.config.ts │ │ ├── eas.json │ │ ├── metro.config.js # Updated for monorepo workspace resolution │ │ ├── package.json # @vineme/mobile │ │ ├── assets/ │ │ ├── plugins/ │ │ ├── ios/ │ │ └── src/ │ └── web/ # Imported vineme-website (full git history preserved) │ ├── next.config.ts │ ├── package.json # @vineme/web │ ├── app/ # Marketing pages + /dashboard/* church admin app │ ├── components/ │ ├── lib/ │ └── public/ # Includes .well-known/ for iOS/Android deep links ├── packages/ │ └── shared/ # @vineme/shared │ ├── package.json │ ├── tsconfig.json │ └── src/ │ ├── index.ts │ └── database.types.ts # Shared Supabase types ├── supabase/ # Shared Supabase migrations, seed.sql, config.toml, functions/ ├── mocks/ # Mock servers + churchsuite-openapi.json ├── scripts/ # Shared repo & DB helper scripts └── docs/ # Consolidated documentation (mobile/ & dashboard/) ``` --- ## 4. Branch & Git History Strategy for `vineme-website` When we fetched `https://github.com/VineMe-App/vineme-website.git`, we inspected all remote branches: - `website/6-qw-1-members-list-stops-at-500-and-search-misses-people` (`b325dd86`) was **already merged into `website/staging`** via PR #61 (`a5ab211c`). - `website/staging` (`a1466961`) also includes **5 additional merged PRs** after `6-qw-1` (#62 Groups search/filter, #63 ChurchSuite Coming Soon, #64/DEV-14 sync users into ChurchSuite, #65 slim Overview banner, #66 group card leaders, #68 one-page layout). - `website/main` (`bb3ab9f0`) has 3 commits for passwordless/phone admin login (`959d3c2b`, `abc2ca3d`, `bb3ab9f0`) that were committed directly to `main` after `staging` branched off. ### How We Preserve 100% of Git History 1. Create a temporary integration branch from `website/staging` (and optionally merge `website/main` into it so no login commits are lost). 2. In that branch, move all `vineme-website` files into `apps/web/` in a single clean commit (`git mv`). 3. Merge that branch into our monorepo branch with `git merge --allow-unrelated-histories`. 4. Every single commit from both repositories remains intact (`git log --follow apps/web/...` and `git blame` will show the full original commit history and authors). --- ## 5. Step-by-Step Execution Plan ### Phase 1: Base Branch & Repo Cleanup 1. Create a dedicated branch (e.g., `chore/monorepo-setup`) from your desired base (`dev` or current `HEAD`). 2. Remove the 39 orphaned hash-named `.svg`/`.png` files, `doc/`, `supabase/doc/`, and `cursor_github_issues_creation.md`. 3. Move `churchsuite-openapi.json` to `mocks/churchsuite-openapi.json` and `FONT_SETUP.md` to `docs/mobile/FONT_SETUP.md`. ### Phase 2: Move Mobile App to `apps/mobile` 1. Use `git mv` to relocate the Expo app files (`src/`, `assets/`, `ios/`, `plugins/`, `app.config.ts`, `babel.config.js`, `eas.json`, `jest.config.js`, `metro.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, `.eslintrc.json`, `package.json`) into `apps/mobile/`. 2. Update `apps/mobile/metro.config.js` for monorepo watchFolders and `nodeModulesPaths` (standard Expo SDK 54 monorepo config). 3. Update `apps/mobile/package.json` name to `@vineme/mobile` and clean up misplaced dependencies. ### Phase 3: Import `vineme-website` into `apps/web` with Full Git History 1. Prepare the `website` history branch with files relocated under `apps/web/`. 2. Merge into the monorepo branch with `--allow-unrelated-histories`. 3. Move `public/.well-known` and `public/auth` into `apps/web/public/`. 4. Rename `apps/web/package.json` to `@vineme/web`. ### Phase 4: Create `packages/shared` & Root Workspace Config 1. Create `packages/shared` (`@vineme/shared`) exporting shared database types and constants. 2. Create root `package.json` with `"workspaces": ["apps/*", "packages/*"]` and root scripts (`dev:mobile`, `dev:web`, `build:web`, `lint`, `test`, `db:types`, `cron:*`). 3. Add `turbo.json` (optional/lightweight) or npm workspace scripts so you can run both apps easily. 4. Update `.gitignore` and `.github/workflows/test.yml` for the monorepo structure. ### Phase 5: Verification 1. Run `npm install` at the workspace root and verify clean dependency resolution (no React version conflicts). 2. Run TypeScript typechecking (`tsc --noEmit`) in both `apps/mobile` and `apps/web`. 3. Run unit tests in `apps/mobile` and a build/lint check in `apps/web`. --- ## 6. Open Questions Before We Execute 1. **Base branch for `vineme2.0`**: You are currently on `fix-at-capacity-text-display` (which has 12 local commits ahead of `origin/fix-at-capacity-text-display`, including `dev-impersonate-user` and merges from `issue-337` and `BUILD26_Churchsuite`). Should we branch off your current `HEAD`, or off `origin/dev`? 2. **Branch for `vineme-website`**: Since `website/staging` already includes `6-qw-1-members-list-stops-at-500-and-search-misses-people` plus 5 newer dashboard PRs (#62–#68), should we import `website/staging` (and also merge the 3 login commits from `website/main`), or strictly stop at `6-qw-1`? 3. **Package Manager**: Both repos currently use **npm** (`package-lock.json`). Would you like to stick with **npm workspaces** (simplest transition, zero new tooling required), or switch to **pnpm**?

## Description

As a maintainer, I want the Prism mock and Vale images in CI pinned by digest, so that a moved tag can't change what the pipeline runs without a pull request saying so.

The `contract` job runs `stoplight/prism:5 mock ...` with a tag only. `hush-hush-php` pins the same image as `stoplight/prism:5@sha256:3f6d29e31bfe0b99587f0f6f79c423858dd6a2ea7e1e4658273ed930a78a9acf`, so this repo is the one that lacks what a sibling already has. That digest is what the `5` tag points at today.

`scripts/lint-vale.sh` sets `VERSION=v3.17.1` and `IMAGE="jdkato/vale:$VERSION"`, a tag with no digest and no `# renovate: datasource=docker depName=jdkato/vale` comment, so nothing bumps it and a moved tag changes the run silently (`rules/markdown.md`, "Running Vale"; `rules/dependencies.md`).

## Acceptance criteria

- Given the `contract` job, then it runs `stoplight/prism:5@sha256:3f6d29e31bfe0b99587f0f6f79c423858dd6a2ea7e1e4658273ed930a78a9acf`, the same reference `hush-hush-php` uses.
- Given `scripts/lint-vale.sh`, then `IMAGE` is `jdkato/vale:v3.17.1@sha256:7dba3c9104ba366f172d119022c4ec53a005f7d14dc1b80e285421a3f0b71657` with the Renovate comment, and no separate `VERSION` is left.
- Given a machine with Docker and no `vale`, when the script runs, then it runs that image and exits 0 on the repo's own docs.
- Given `actionlint` and the repo's lints, then they pass.

## Definition of done

- The change made and the repo's own checks passing; pull request linked with `Closes #<this>`, and this issue closed referencing it.

Found by auditing the SDK repos against the global rules on 2026-10-03. Read for this ticket: [jdkato/vale on Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/jdkato/vale).

## 背景

Schema SBI の OpenAPI 検証では Prism Mock を使って対象 endpoint の response を確認する方針です。

現在は認証付き endpoint に `Authorization` header を付けて Mock request すると Security 判定で停止するため、認証付き endpoint しか変更しない Schema SBI では Prism で1件も request できず、`checked = 0` となって fail-closed します。

この状態で `checked = 0` を PASS にしたり、人間承認だけで Mock 確認を免除するのではなく、Prism 専用の Trusted Verifier で固定の dummy credential だけを許可し、認証付き endpoint も contract verification できるようにします。

関連: #91, #95

## 方針

- 認証付き endpoint でも Prism Mock request を実行する
- `Authorization: Bearer <fixed dummy token>` のような固定 dummy 値だけを許可する
- 実 Secret / 実 JWT / 実 Credential は使用禁止
- Prism Mock のための Trusted Verifier として明示的に隔離する
- Security Gate の人間承認を「Mock 確認を省略する仕組み」としては使わない
- 1件も確認できなかった場合は引き続き fail-closed とする

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 認証付き OpenAPI endpoint を Prism に対して最低1件 request できる
- [ ] request に使用できる Authorization は固定 dummy Bearer token のみ
- [ ] 実 Secret / 実 JWT / 実 Credential が渡された場合は FAIL する
- [ ] 対象 endpoint の expected status code を検証する
- [ ] response body を OpenAPI schema / example と照合できる
- [ ] `checked.length === 0` の場合は FAIL する
- [ ] checked / skipped endpoint と理由を verification result から追跡できる
- [ ] 認証付き endpoint しか存在しない Schema SBI でも Prism Mock verification を完了できる
- [ ] Security Gate の承認だけで Mock verification を SKIP / PASS できない

## 非ゴール

- Cognito など実認証 Provider との接続確認
- 実 JWT の署名検証
- 本番 Credential を使った E2E 認証テスト

## 現時点の運用

この Issue が完了するまでは、認証付き endpoint だけの Schema SBI は Prism で1件も確認できない場合 FAIL のままとし、`checked = 0` を例外的に PASS にはしない。

#95 は #91 を自動 close せず `Refs #91` とし、#91 はこの対応を含む必要な follow-up が完了するまで open のままにする。
title: Prism Mockで認証付きendpointをdummy Bearer tokenで検証できるようにする

## 背景

現在はAPI Schema Planner系の専用CLIとして `planner:api-schema` / `planner:api-schema-approve` があり、通常SBIとは別系統のフローになっている。

一方、SONOMAMAではSBIの粒度を小さく保ち、PBI配下に「OpenAPI Schemaを作るSBI」を1つ置く運用を想定している。

例:

```text
PBI: 受講生一覧機能を作る
├─ SBI: OpenAPI Schemaを作る
├─ SBI: Rails APIを実装する
├─ SBI: Admin画面を実装する
└─ SBI: 結合確認する
```

Schema作成も通常SBIとして扱えば、人間向けにAPI Schema専用コマンドや別承認フローを持つ必要がなくなる。

## 目的

OpenAPI Schema作成を通常SBIフローへ統合し、Schema SBIでは以下までを1つの作業単位として完了させる。

- `packages/api-schema/openapi.yaml` の作成/更新
- OpenAPI validation / contract check
- Prism Mock起動確認
- 想定responseの確認
- PR自動作成
- Human PR Review

## 目標フロー

```text
GitHub Issue (PBI)
↓
pnpm planner:sbi PBI_URL
↓
AIがSBIへ分割
↓
API契約変更が必要なら「OpenAPI Schema作成SBI」を生成
↓
Human Review / ready
↓
pnpm harness:run SCHEMA_SBI_URL
↓
OpenAPI作成/更新
↓
OpenAPI validation / contract check
↓
Prism Mock起動・response確認
↓
Local Verification PASS
↓
AI/HarnessがPR自動作成
↓
Human PR Review / Merge
↓
後続のRails / Frontend SBIが実装開始可能
```

## 実装方針

- `planner:sbi` がPBIを分割するとき、API契約の新規作成/変更が必要ならSchema作成SBIを通常SBIとして生成する
- Schema SBIは通常の `sbi` / `needs-review` / `ready` フローを使う
- Schema SBIも `pnpm harness:run SBI_URL` で実行する
- Schema SBIのExecutionではOpenAPI作成/更新に必要な内部処理をHarness/AIが実行する
- 既存のAPI Schema Planner実装は必要なら内部機能として再利用してよいが、人間向けの独立フローにはしない
- `planner:api-schema` / `planner:api-schema-approve` は通常開発者向けpackage script / Quick Startから外す

#91（PR #95）のSchema SBIでは、Prism Mockで最低1件のendpointをrequestできなければFAILにしている。ただし認証付きendpointはrequestしていない。Authorization headerを送るテストコードがHarnessのSecurity判定（SEC-AUTH）に当たるためで、Harness側の都合による制約。

その結果、認証付きendpointだけを変えるSchema SBIは、現在は0件確認でFAILしPRを作れない（fail-closedのまま止まるのは意図どおり）。

Security Gate（Human Gate）を通したらMock確認を免除する、という解決はしない。Human Gateは危険な変更を承認する仕組みであって、本来できるcontract verificationを省略する仕組みではないため。

## 目的

認証付きOpenAPI endpointも、Trustedな検証経路でPrism Mockへrequestし、contractを確認できるようにする。

## 方針

```text
認証付きSchema
↓
TrustedなPrism Mock verifier（.harness/verification/** 側、Agent書込禁止）
↓
固定のdummy Bearer token
↓
Prismへrequest
↓
status / response schema確認
```

- dummy Bearerは固定値で、実Credentialとの区別が機械的にできるものにする。
- Agent生成コードやApplication Testに認証headerの送信を許可する方向（SEC-AUTH判定の緩和）では解決しない。

- [ ] requestしたendpointが0件ならFAILのまま

本Issueの完了をもって #91 をcloseする。

## 背景

当前架构聚焦于**黑盒 E2E（Playwright POM）与接口层（pytest + requests + PostgreSQL 断言）**，测试金字塔的上层已覆盖，但以下三类专项测试尚未集成。

## 现状盘点

| 能力 | 现状 | 证据 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 单元测试 | ❌ 缺失 | `tests/` 下仅有 `api/`、`web/`、`mobile/`、`perf/`，无 `tests/unit/` |
| 白盒代码覆盖率 | ❌ 缺失 | `requirements.txt` 无 `pytest-cov` / `coverage`；`.github/workflows/ci.yml` 无覆盖率步骤与阈值门禁 |
| DAST 动态安全扫描 | ❌ 缺失 | 无 OWASP ZAP / Nikto / nuclei 相关配置或 CI 步骤 |
| 前端视觉回归 | ❌ 缺失 | `tests/web/` 中无 `to_have_screenshot` / 基线截图对比逻辑 |
| 可访问性扫描 | ❌ 缺失 | 无 axe-core / `@axe-core/playwright` 接入 |

`ci.yml` 的 5 个执行步骤分别为：启动基础设施 → 构建运行时 → API 测试 → Web 测试 → k6 压测，未包含任何安全 / 覆盖率 / 视觉回归环节。

## 影响

1. **反馈链路偏长**：缺少单元测试意味着缺陷只能在 E2E 层暴露，定位成本高、执行耗时长，违背测试金字塔「快速反馈」原则。
2. **覆盖率不可见**：无法量化测试对被测代码的覆盖程度，也就无法回答「测试是否足够」。
3. **安全左移缺位**：接口与前端的安全问题（注入、越权、敏感信息泄露、缺失安全响应头）没有任何自动化检测手段。
4. **UI 回归靠肉眼**：CSS / 布局类回归只能依赖人工比对，CI 无法拦截。

## 建议方案

**1. 白盒覆盖率（优先级最高，成本最低）**

- `requirements.txt` 增加 `pytest-cov`
- `ci.yml` 中 `pytest` 步骤追加 `--cov=... --cov-report=xml --cov-report=term-missing`
- 覆盖率产物上传为 artifact，并设置初始阈值门禁（如 line coverage ≥ 60%，后续逐步抬高）
- 若被测代码不在本仓库内，可先对 `tests/web/pages/` 等 POM 封装层与 `conftest.py` 建立覆盖率基线

**2. 单元测试层**

- 新增 `tests/unit/`，覆盖 POM 基类、测试数据构造、工具函数、配置加载等纯逻辑
- 与 E2E 分层执行，CI 中作为快速失败的第一道关卡

**3. DAST 动态安全扫描**

- 引入 OWASP ZAP，以 `zaproxy/zap-stable` 容器方式接入 `qa-infra-net`，对 Prism Mock / 被测服务执行 baseline scan
- 新增 `tests/security/` 目录与独立 CI job（可设为非阻塞，先观察再收紧）
- 产出 ZAP 报告并上传 artifact

**4. 前端视觉回归**

- Playwright 已内置 `expect(page).to_have_screenshot()`，无需额外框架
- 对关键页面建立基线截图，配置 `maxDiffPixelRatio` 容忍度
- 注意：基线截图受字体渲染影响，需固定容器内字体环境（当前镜像已满足）

**5. 可访问性扫描（可选加分项）**

- 接入 `@axe-core/playwright`，在现有 Web 用例中断言无严重级别违规

## 验收标准

- [ ] `pytest --cov` 可执行，CI 输出覆盖率报告并设置阈值门禁
- [ ] 新增 `tests/unit/` 目录并有实际用例
- [ ] CI 中存在 DAST job（可先非阻塞）并产出报告 artifact
- [ ] 至少一个关键页面接入视觉回归基线
- [ ] README 的架构层级表补充对应工具与目录映射

body:
**Describe the bug** When a response schema has `nullable: true` without a sibling `type`, Respect's schema check doesn't validate the response. It fails with an Ajv error, whatever the response is: ``` Ajv error: "nullable" cannot be used without "type" ``` OpenAPI 3.0 doesn't forbid this. `nullable` "adds "null" to the allowed type specified by the type keyword, only if type is explicitly defined within the same Schema Object", so without `type` it has no effect. #925 reached the same conclusion: "there is nothing in the spec that says you can't use `nullable` without a `type`". That's why `lint` reports it through its own rule, `nullable-type-sibling`, which can be turned off. Respect has no way around it. The error is thrown when `@redocly/ajv` compiles the schema (the same message as the `lint` crash in #319), so a description that passes `lint` with `nullable-type-sibling: off` still can't be checked by Respect. It also fails on `nullable: true` next to `allOf`, which code generators emit (examples in #925), for instance `note: { nullable: true, allOf: [ { type: string } ] }`. Other OpenAPI response validators accept the response (below). **To Reproduce** The script writes an OpenAPI description, an Arazzo workflow and a response body into a temp dir, serves the body on `localhost:8080` with node, and runs Respect (needs only `node`/`npx`): ```sh #!/bin/sh set -u cd "$(mktemp -d)" cat > openapi.yaml <<'EOF' openapi: 3.0.3 info: { title: nullable-without-type, version: 1.0.0 } servers: [ { url: 'http://localhost:8080' } ] paths: /note: get: operationId: getNote responses: '200': description: ok content: application/json: schema: type: object properties: note: { nullable: true } EOF cat > arazzo.yaml <<'EOF' arazzo: 1.0.1 info: { title: nullable-without-type, version: 1.0.0 } sourceDescriptions: - { name: api, url: ./openapi.yaml, type: openapi } workflows: - workflowId: getNote steps: - stepId: getNote operationId: getNote successCriteria: - condition: $statusCode == 200 EOF echo '{"note":null}' > body.json version=${REDOCLY_CLI_VERSION:-2.78.0} node -e ' const body = require("fs").readFileSync("body.json"); require("http").createServer((req, res) => { res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "application/json" }); res.end(body); }).listen(8080); ' & mock=$! trap 'kill $mock' EXIT until node -e 'fetch("http://localhost:8080").then(() => process.exit(0), () => process.exit(1))'; do sleep 0.2; done npx --yes "@redocly/cli@$version" respect arazzo.yaml ``` **Expected behavior** The schema check validates the response. `nullable` without `type` has no effect, so here it passes: `note` accepts any value. If Respect should warn about the schema, a message that doesn't fail the check, or one that can be turned off like the lint rule. **Logs** ``` ✗ GET /note - step getNote ✓ success criteria check - $statusCode == 200 ✓ status code check - $statusCode in [200] ✓ content-type check ✗ schema check stepId - getNote ✗ schema check Ajv error: "nullable" cannot be used without "type" ``` **Other tools** The same description and response, through OpenAPI response validators: | Tool | Result | |---|---| | Respect 2.78.0 | fails: `Ajv error: "nullable" cannot be used without "type"` | | openapi-core 0.23.1 | valid | | Schemathesis 4.33.4 (`response_schema_conformance`) | no issues | | Prism 5.14.2 (validation proxy) | no violations |
others.sh: the same check with openapi-core, Schemathesis and Prism (needs Docker; run it in the directory the script above creates) ```sh #!/bin/sh # Run from a repro directory: checks body.json against openapi.yaml with openapi-core, Schemathesis # and Prism, each in Docker, sharing the mock container's network so localhost:8080 is the mock. set -u tools=${*:-openapi-core schemathesis prism} mock=repro-mock-$$ docker run --detach --rm --name "$mock" --volume "$PWD:/r:ro" --workdir /r node:22-slim node -e ' const body = require("fs").readFileSync("body.json"); require("http").createServer((req, res) => { res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "application/json" }); res.end(body); }).listen(8080); ' >/dev/null || exit trap 'docker stop "$mock" >/dev/null' EXIT tool() { docker run --rm --network "container:$mock" --volume "$PWD:/r:ro" --workdir /r "$@"; } path=$(sed -n 's|^ \(/[^:]*\):.*|\1|p' openapi.yaml | head -n 1) summary= for t in $tools; do echo "=== $t" case $t in openapi-core) tool --interactive python:3.12-slim sh -c ' pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check --root-user-action=ignore openapi-core==0.23.1 requests==2.32.5 python - "$0"' "$path" <<'EOF' import sys, requests from openapi_core import OpenAPI from openapi_core.contrib.requests import RequestsOpenAPIRequest, RequestsOpenAPIResponse request = requests.Request("GET", "http://localhost:8080" + sys.argv[1]) response = requests.Session().send(request.prepare()) print(sys.argv[1], response.status_code, response.text) try: OpenAPI.from_file_path("openapi.yaml").validate_response(RequestsOpenAPIRequest(request), RequestsOpenAPIResponse(response)) print("valid") except Exception as e: print("invalid:", e, e.__cause__ or "") sys.exit(1) EOF ;; schemathesis) tool --workdir /tmp schemathesis/schemathesis:v4.33.4 run /r/openapi.yaml --url http://localhost:8080 --checks response_schema_conformance --phases examples,coverage --no-color ;; prism) tool node:22-slim sh -c ' npx --yes @stoplight/prism-cli@5.14.2 proxy openapi.yaml http://localhost:8080 --port 4010 >/tmp/prism.log 2>&1 & until grep -q "Prism is listening" /tmp/prism.log; do sleep 0.5; done node -e " fetch(\"http://localhost:4010$0\").then(async r => { const violations = r.headers.get(\"sl-violations\"); console.log(\"$0\", r.status, await r.text()); console.log(violations ? \"violations: \" + violations : \"no violations\"); process.exit(violations ? 1 : 0); }); "' "$path" ;; *) echo "unknown tool: $t (openapi-core, schemathesis, prism)" >&2; false ;; esac status=$? summary="$summary$(printf '%-14s %s' "$t" "$([ $status -eq 0 ] && echo accepts || echo "rejects (exit $status)")") " done printf '\n%s' "$summary" ```

body:
## Problem

The resource tests in `test/e_invoice_api/resources/` run against a Prism mock server. `scripts/mock` starts this server. By default, it gets the live spec from `https://api.e-invoice.be/api/openapi.json`. The `OPENAPI_SPEC_URL` variable can change the spec, but CI does not set it.

Thus, CI can stop with an error when there is no change in the code:

- When the API changes, the mock gives responses that are different from the SDK models.
- When the API is not available, Prism cannot start. CI sets `PRISM_MOCK=1`, so the test job stops with an error.

Also, the result of a CI run on an old commit can change with time. This makes it difficult to compare test runs.

## Proposal

This is a proposal. The team must agree on it before the work starts.

1. Keep a copy of the spec in the repo, for example `openapi.json` in the root or in `scripts/`.
2. In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, set `OPENAPI_SPEC_URL` to the path of the copy in the `test` job.
3. Add a scheduled workflow that compares the copy with the live spec.
4. When the two specs are different, the scheduled workflow stops with an error, or it opens an issue.
5. When we sync the SDK with the API, we update the copy in the same pull request.

Questions for the team:

- Which location do we use for the copy?
- Must the scheduled workflow stop with an error, or must it open an issue?
- How frequently must the scheduled workflow run?

## Procedure

Do these steps only after the team agrees on the proposal.

1. Download the live spec to the location that the team selects.
2. In the `test` job of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, set `OPENAPI_SPEC_URL` to the path of the copy.
3. Add a new workflow file in `.github/workflows/` with a `schedule` trigger.
4. In the new workflow, download the live spec and compare it with the copy.
5. In the new workflow, give a clear message that shows the difference.
6. In `CONTRIBUTING.md`, tell how to update the copy.
7. Add the same step to the sync procedure in `SYNC-AND-RELEASE.md` when this file is in the repo.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The team agrees on the proposal, or closes this issue.
- [ ] The CI `test` job does not connect to `api.e-invoice.be`.
- [ ] The scheduled workflow shows a difference between the copy and the live spec.
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` tells how to update the copy.
